agent_notes: Verse 8 gives no time. Placed between the altar and the second theophany by verse order, 3 days after the altar, with a 3-day margin; DAY_SEQUENCE like the surrounding Bethel scenes (the text has no time word of its own, so the tier is that of the scene it falls in). Pseudo-Jonathan places the theophany after Rebekah's death (news arriving), which is not modelled.

history.note: [should_fix] Set precision_tier to DAY_SEQUENCE like the other Bethel events, keep the ±3-day margin, and change the temporal_reasoning_note so it no longer says MACRO_ERA. (GEN.35.8: "But Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Beth-el" (no time word, placed between 35:7 and 35:9 at Bethel))

agent_notes: Verse 9 says 'again, when he came from Paddan-aram'. Taken as a second theophany at Bethel itself, soon after the altar (v. 7), not as a later visit. The ordering after Deborah's burial follows verse order only.
Anchored 1 day after the rebuke at Shechem with a 2-day margin; the text has no time word. Ch. 34 events are at day level, so the chain stays DAY_SEQUENCE.
The promise of kings and of the land (35:11-12) will likely be fulfilled in later chapters (Gen 46:3, Exod, Joshua, Samuel); those chapters' sessions write the links.

Isaac's 180 years are dated from anchor.isaac_birth (180 years, c. 1886 BCE, 12 years after Joseph's sale at 17, Gen 37:2). Ramban on 35:28 (after Rashi): the Torah does not keep strict order here; Isaac's death follows the sale of Joseph in time, though it is told before it. So this event is told here but falls after the Joseph events of Gen 37-40 in time. Jacob was then 120, Joseph 29 (Gen 41:46 puts Joseph at 30 on standing before Pharaoh).

No interval stated. Jacob is at Hebron by Gen 37:14 (Joseph aged 17, c. 1898 BCE on the anchors), so the 6-month offset with a 6-month margin stays well before that. Travel Migdal-eder to Hebron is ~24 km straight, about a day by donkey. Joseph is about 12-13 at Gen 34 (c. 1903 BCE), so the chain fits.

[consider] Consider a morning time_of_day on the departure so the hours downstream don't fall at night. (GEN.35.5: "And they journeyed"; urim travel Shechem→Bethel: 41 km by road, donkey 10.2 h moving, ≈1 day)

agent_notes: The text gives no pause length at Bethel. The route to Ephrath/Bethlehem is ~31 km by road (donkey ~7.5 h), 'a little way' short of it; I use 30 hours after the pillar (a day at Bethel plus ~6 h on the road) with a 2-day margin.
Considered a link from the divine promise of 35:11 (a nation, kings) to Benjamin's birth; dropped as not stated.
'When Israel dwelt in that land' gives no interval. 2 months after Migdal-eder with a 2-month margin is a guess to keep the order Eder, Reuben, Hebron. MACRO_ERA.

history.note: [consider] Consider matching the tier to the margin (SEASONAL_MONTH) or widening the margin if the span is meant to be truly open. (GEN.35.22: "when Israel dwelt in that land")

notes.note: Verses 23-26 (the list of Jacob's twelve sons) are left out as an undated genealogical list; 22b ('the sons of Jacob were twelve') is covered by the Reuben event as framing.
